newsitem.title: FRANCE: Air France Europe pilots to strike on April 25.
newsitem.headline: Air France Europe pilots to strike on April 25.

text.p: Four unions representing cockpit crews at airline Air France Europe said on Tuesday they have called a 48-hour strike starting on April 25.
The strike call at the domestic and regional airline of the state-owned Air France group follows a stoppage over Easter weekend which the airline estimated lost it 121,500 passengers.

The USPNT, SPAF, SNPL and SNPNAC unions said in a statement they are protesting against chairman Christian Blanc's decision to present a plan to the board to integrate Air France Europe crews into the Air France international company.

"Stuck in his systematic policy of presenting a fait accompli and contrary to his promises, chairman Christian Blanc has announced his plan to submit to the Air France board on 24 April 1997, a text envisaging a discriminatory treatment in integrating Air France Europe pilots," the joint statement said.

Blanc is preparing a merger of the two airlines to ready the group for privatisation and improve competitiveness. The plan would put Air France Europe crews on the same pay scale and rosters as Air France counterparts, involving a pay-cut of around 15 percent.
Apart from the Air France Europe action, employees of two other French airlines are on strike, TAT and Air Liberte, both subsidiaries of British Airways Plc.

Cockpit crew unions at those two companies were nearing an agreement on Tuesday after stoppages grounded around half their flights over the past two weeks. They have been in dispute over merger plans and work conditions.
